approach: Add an early step at verification start in `Athena::go` (in the verification part of `produce_and_verify`, right after `closing.candidate` is set at the end of admission and before `verifier_snapshot`). The step pushes the candidate commit to `work_branch(job)` and opens the job's PR through the `Remote` and `PrHost` seams, never merging. The logic lives in a new generic function in gh.rs, `open_early_pr`, testable with fakes. An `Athena::early_pr` wrapper finds `origin`, applies `parse_remote`, and returns silently if there is no origin or it is not GitHub. Otherwise it builds `GhCli`, `GhClient` and `GitRemote` itself, so the `go` signature is unchanged. Any error becomes one `warning:` line and the job goes on. The early head is stored in a new state-dir file via pr.rs. `land_pr` then reuses the stored link (no second `open_pr`). If the remote branch still holds exactly the stored early head, it replaces it with the landing commit through a new `Remote::replace` (`--force-with-lease` pinned to that head), guarded by `check_replace`. It sets `link.head` to the landing commit before the existing head check and merges guarded with that commit. A cfg(test) thread-local seam supplies fake Remote/PrHost to the production wrapper so tests can drive real `go`.

decisions.choice: Add `Remote::replace(branch, commit, expected_old)` with a default body that returns an error; `GitRemote` overrides it with `git push --force-with-lease=refs/heads/<b>:<old>`.
decisions.reason: The landing commit L is built from the user's head and does not descend from the candidate, so a plain push after the early push would be refused. `check_replace` already exists in pr.rs for this. The default body keeps the `Remote` impl in athena-cli/tests/external_calls.rs compiling.

rejected.why: Breaks the external_calls.rs impl, which is not a deliverable.
Not lease-pinned; could clobber a fix pushed by someone else.

decisions.choice: Record the early head in a separate state-dir file (`pr-early.json`) with `store_early`/`load_early` in pr.rs; leave `PrLink` and `LandPr` unchanged.
decisions.reason: `land_pr` replaces only when the remote head equals the head Athena itself pushed early. Any other head is still refused as today. Adding fields to `PrLink` or `LandPr` would break struct literals in external_calls.rs and elsewhere.

rejected.why: Breaks existing literals; link.head is also overwritten by land_pr.
Would discard a user's fix; existing refusal tests forbid it.

decisions.choice: The test seam is a `#[cfg(test)]` thread-local in gh.rs that holds fake `Remote` and `PrHost` objects, which `Athena::early_pr` uses instead of building the real GitHub client. Production code has no hook.
decisions.reason: `Athena::go` and the CLI signatures are unchanged and Athena has no injectable host field (adding one breaks every `Athena { .. }` literal). The thread-local lets a real `go` run against fakes.

rejected.why: Breaks the literals in run_pin_tests, reconcile, invocation, introspect, steward and the CLI.
Would not show that `go` itself triggers the step.

decisions.choice: Skip silently when `git remote get-url origin` fails or `parse_remote` returns Err. Print `warning: ...` only when the step fails on a GitHub remote. Never propagate the error.
decisions.reason: Matches criteria 2 and 4. Local-only repos and the existing CLI lifecycle tests (path origins) must show no new 'warning' line.

rejected.option: Warn on a non-GitHub origin too

decisions.choice: Early step: if a stored link exists, only replace the head (lease-pinned) and update the link. Otherwise push (new branch) and `open_pr`, then store the link and the early head. A rerun of the early step with the branch at the same commit does nothing.
decisions.reason: Gives 'open or update' and avoids a second PR on retry.

decisions.choice: Tests and docs use https://github.com/owner/repo URLs only, and any identity comes from existing git config. Changelog gets one entry.

rejected.option: SSH-style remotes in the gh.rs parse tests

files.purpose: Add `Remote::replace` (default body is an error) and the `GitRemote` override with `--force-with-lease`. Add `open_early_pr` (generic over Remote/PrHost). Add `Athena::early_pr` (origin lookup, silent skip, builds `GhCli`, warning on error). Add the cfg(test) seam. Change `land_pr` to replace an early head with the landing commit via `check_replace`. Add FakeRemote.replace recording and new tests.
Add `store_early`/`load_early` for the early head file in the job's state dir, plus unit tests.
Call `self.early_pr(...)` in `produce_and_verify` after admission and before `verifier_snapshot`, ignoring its result. Add core tests for the criteria 1, 2 and 4 cases.
Doc and module-text update only if the landing description needs the replace step; otherwise limited to a comment.
Add a recording fake remote/host pair and a helper that runs `go` with the seam installed.
Assert that existing lifecycle runs print no 'warning' line from the early step.
Add the entry required by criterion 8.

steps: gh.rs: add `Remote::replace` with a default error body; implement it in `GitRemote` with `--force-with-lease=refs/heads/<b>:<old>`; update the FakeRemote in tests to record replaces.

gh.rs: write `open_early_pr(state, job, branch, commit, remote, host, ancestry, pr draft, host_name, repository)`: read the remote head; no link: `check_push`, push, `default_branch`, `open_pr`, store link and early head; link exists and the head differs: `check_replace`, `replace`, update link head and early head. Return Result.

gh.rs: add `Athena::early_pr(ctx data, candidate commit, ui)`. It runs `git remote get-url origin`, then `parse_remote`; either failing returns silently. Otherwise it builds `GhCli`/`GhClient`/`GitRemote` (or the cfg(test) seam) and calls `open_early_pr`. An Err prints one `warning: could not open the pull request early: ...` line; nothing is propagated.

gh.rs `land_pr`: when the link is open and the remote head differs from `job.commit`, and `load_early` equals that remote head, run `check_replace`, then `remote.replace(branch, commit, &head)`, set `link.head = job.commit`, store the link, clear the early file, then continue into the existing head check. Any other head still gets the refusal text.
run.rs: call `self.early_pr(...)` after `closing.candidate = Some(candidate)` at the end of admission and before `verifier_snapshot`, ignoring errors. Skip it when `self.nested.is_some()`.

Add tests: gh.rs land tests (criterion 3), run.rs `go` tests with the seam (criteria 1, 2, 4), plus a lifecycle.rs assertion that no output has 'warning'. Confirm each fails with the new code removed.
CHANGELOG.md entry; check land.rs comments; run cargo fmt, clippy (`--all-targets --locked -D warnings`) and `cargo test --workspace`; scan the diff for email-like text.

risks.risk: The early push sends a commit with no records or trailers to a public branch.
risks.mitigation: It is the job's own `athena/<job>` branch only (`check_push` and `check_replace` enforce the branch name). Landing replaces it with L, and the lease pin protects against third-party pushes.

risks.risk: The early step adds latency or hangs on network calls.
risks.mitigation: It runs once, its errors are non-fatal, and the existing `GhClient` retry bounds apply.

risks.risk: The cfg(test) thread-local leaks between tests.
risks.mitigation: Use an RAII guard that clears it on drop, and give each test its own thread (the default in cargo test).

risks.risk: Replacing a remote head with a lease fails if the remote moved.
risks.mitigation: The lease failure becomes the usual landing error and nothing is merged; the same refusal text as today is preserved for foreign heads.

risks.risk: CLI lifecycle tests that use path origins break.
risks.mitigation: A path origin fails `parse_remote` and is skipped silently with no output.

demonstrations.method: Core test drives a real `Athena::go` (using the `make_athena` fake-driver rig in test_support.rs, with a small go-fixture helper added there) with the cfg(test) seam holding a recording FakeRemote and FakeHost. The fake host records `open_pr` and `merge`.
demonstrations.observes: Before `go` returns, the FakeRemote saw one push (or replace) of the candidate commit to `athena/<job>`, the FakeHost saw one `open_pr` with head `athena/<job>`, and `merge` was never called. The recorded events show the push happened before verification finished (before the verification record was written).
demonstrations.fails_without: With the early step removed, the fakes record no push and no open_pr, so the assertions fail.

demonstrations.method: Two `go` runs on identical fixtures: one with working fakes and one where the push errors, and a third where `open_pr` errors. Compare the outcome state, reason and landed result.
demonstrations.observes: The outcome of the failing runs equals the no-failure run (same state and same landing), and the only difference is a `warning:` line in the UI output.
demonstrations.fails_without: If errors were propagated, `go` would return Err or a failed outcome and the equality assertion would fail.

demonstrations.method: New gh.rs test with FakeRemote (records `replace` calls and the expected-old argument), FakeHost and Rig. Store an early link and early head E, put E on the remote, then run `land_pr` with landing commit L. Also a test for the head not equal to E, and another using a spy ancestry to show `check_replace` ran.
demonstrations.observes: `open_pr` count is 0 for this run; one `replace(branch, L, E)` was made; the stored link.head is L; the head check passes; `merge_heads == ["L"]`. For a remote head X that is neither E nor L, nothing is replaced and the existing refusal text is returned.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the replace path the remote head E != L hits the existing refusal and `land_pr` errors, or `open_pr` is called twice.

demonstrations.method: Core test runs `go` with no origin, and another with a path origin (non-GitHub), collecting UI lines. Another test with the seam installed on a GitHub-parsed remote and a failing host shows the warning appears there. The CLI lifecycle tests in athena-cli/tests/lifecycle.rs get an assertion that no output line contains 'warning'.
demonstrations.observes: No UI line contains 'warning' for no-origin and non-GitHub origins; exactly one warning line appears only for a host error on a GitHub remote.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the step warned or errored on a missing/non-GitHub origin, the no-'warning' assertion fails.

demonstrations.method: Run the whole workspace tests, then `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`. Each new test was written to fail against the base (the early step absent or the replace path absent).
demonstrations.observes: All three commands exit 0 with no warnings, and the existing CLI lifecycle tests still pass with no new 'warning' line.
demonstrations.fails_without: A new test that does not exercise the new behavior would pass against the base; reviewers confirm each asserts a push, open_pr, replace or skipped call that the base cannot produce.

demonstrations.method: Inspect the full diff for `@` followed by a host name pattern or SSH-style `user@host:owner/repo` remotes, in source, tests and CHANGELOG.
demonstrations.observes: Added lines contain only https://github.com/owner/repo URLs and no email-like text.

demonstrations.method: Check the diff of run.rs: the `go` signature `go(&self, job_ref, accepted_by, ui)` is unchanged, `crates/athena-cli` has no src change, and `Athena::early_pr` constructs `GhCli` itself.
demonstrations.observes: No signature or CLI call-site hunk in the diff; `GhCli` is constructed inside the early-step wrapper.

The new entry says verification start opens or updates the job's PR so CI caches by fingerprint, that it never merges, that a missing or non-GitHub origin is skipped quietly, and that failures are non-fatal.

The exact UI output line used for the warning must start with 'warning:' like the existing ones; whether the CLI lifecycle tests already contain an unrelated 'warning' line I did not read.
Whether `gh api` open_pr fails when a PR for the branch already exists; the plan avoids a second call by relying on the stored link.
